column1: # Calibration set for the end-of-turn threshold (T2).
# Twenty utterances in three families, interleaved on purpose: ten of the same
# kind in a row and the speaker settles into one prosody, which is the one thing
# this set must not measure.
#   fini        the turn is over, ARIA must answer
#   hesitation  the speaker is still holding the floor: filler, lengthened
#               vowel, pitch held up. ARIA must wait
#   coupure     the speaker stops dead mid-phrase, no filler, no trailing off.
#               ARIA must wait — and this is the hard family, because a clean
#               cut and a finished sentence differ by **syntax**, which a
#               waveform-only detector cannot see
# Record in this order, one file per line:
#   cargo run --release -p aria-voice --bin dictate -- --save
# PROTOCOL — it decides whether the numbers mean anything.
#  1. **Intonation carries the label, not the text.** An ellipsis on the page
#     suspends nothing: if the voice falls on the last word, the utterance IS
#     finished, and both the turn model and the ASR will say so. Three of the
#     first twenty recordings died there — the ASR even wrote "de" as "d'eux."
#     with a full stop, because that is genuinely what was said.
#       - fini: let the voice fall, normally.
#       - hesitation: lengthen the last syllable, keep the pitch UP, add the
#         filler if it comes naturally.
#       - coupure: stop dead, as if cut off — and above all **do not let the
#         voice fall** on the last word. No ellipsis is written on those lines
#         precisely so nothing invites trailing off.
#  2. **Wait about one second of silence before pressing Enter.** The model
#     judges the end of the stream: a recording cut at the instant the voice
#     stops reads as "finished" whatever was said.
#  3. One utterance per file. The index below is the file number.
# Then score the set:
#   cargo run --release -p aria-voice --bin turn -- --set
# index
